subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Who Drinks the Most Coffee?
description: A quick, practical guide to Who Drinks the Most Coffee?.

hook.text: The USA is the world's largest total coffee consumer. But per capita, it doesn't even crack the top 10.

buildup.text: Nordic countries dominate per-capita consumption. Finland averages 12 kg per person per year—four cups daily.

discovery.text: Long, dark winters and a cultural tradition of 'kahvitauko' (coffee break) drive Finland's astonishing intake.

twist.text: China, historically a tea nation, is the world's fastest-growing coffee market. Starbucks opens a new store there every 15 hours.

climax.text: Global coffee demand grows 2% annually. Supply struggles to keep up, pushing prices upward over time.

punchline.text: Finland drinks the most. China is catching up the fastest.

quiz.question: Which country drinks the most coffee per capita?

details.summary: Scandinavian countries lead global coffee consumption per capita, with Finland averaging about 12 kilograms per person annually. The United States is the largest total consumer by volume. Coffee consumption is growing fastest in Asia, particularly in China, South Korea, and Japan.
details.whyItMatters: Consumption patterns drive global trade flows. As Asian markets grow, they reshape demand, supply chains, and which coffees become commercially valuable.
takeaways: Finland leads per-capita consumption at 12 kg per person per year
The United States is the largest total consumer by volume
Asia is the fastest-growing coffee consumption region

faq.question: Why do Scandinavian countries drink so much coffee?
faq.answer: Long dark winters, a strong social coffee culture called fika in Sweden, and historical trade connections all contribute. Coffee is deeply embedded in daily life and social rituals. The Lutheran work ethic and cold climate may have also played a role historically.

faq.question: Is coffee consumption growing or declining worldwide?
faq.answer: Global consumption grows about 2 percent annually. Growth is strongest in Asia and Africa. Traditional markets in Europe and North America are mature but shifting toward specialty and premium segments. Total world consumption exceeds 10 billion kilograms per year.
